openai/gpt-5.6-sol.title: CRC-16-CCITT starts at 0x0000 instead of the required 0xFFFF, breaking wire interoperability.
MAX_PAYLOAD permits 65536 bytes although P2 limits payloads to 65535 bytes.
Public consume accepts values larger than the unread region and can silently discard data or wrap the cursor.
Consumed prefixes are retained whenever one unread byte remains, allowing repeated next_frame use to grow the allocation without bound.
next_frame never checks that the complete declared frame is buffered before slicing its payload and trailer.
A checksum failure consumes the entire claimed frame instead of resynchronizing at the next magic sequence.
A checksum mismatch is reported as Ok(None) rather than FrameError::Corrupt.
Reentrant feed can make a newly completed frame exceed the stale drain budget and underflow the budget subtraction.
drain discards every parsing error even though malformed frames must surface FrameError to the caller.
Resynchronization discards a trailing 0xA5 byte, corrupting a magic sequence split across feed calls.

fireworks-ai/accounts/fireworks/models/g.title: CRC-16 initial value is 0x0000 but INTENT P1 requires 0xFFFF, so every checksum is wrong versus a compliant peer (K3).
MAX_PAYLOAD is 65536 but INTENT P2 caps payload at 65535; encode and parse both accept a payload one byte over the limit.
next_frame computes frame_len then slices data[HEADER_LEN..HEADER_LEN+len] and indexes the trailer without verifying data.len() >= frame_len, panicking on any partial frame (violates P2 and P5).
Checksum failure returns Ok(None) instead of Err(FrameError::Corrupt), silently dropping malformed input in direct violation of P4.
drain does budget -= consumed without underflow checking; a reentrant handler that feeds new bytes (K2) can make consumed exceed budget, panicking in debug or wrapping in release.
On checksum failure next_frame consumes frame_len instead of resynchronizing at the next magic sequence as P4 requires, so a corrupted length field skips past valid frames.
resync returns data.len() when no magic is found, consuming a trailing 0xA5 that could be the first byte of a split magic sequence, violating P6 preservation of partial frames.
feed computes self.available() + chunk.len() without overflow checking; on 32-bit a large attacker-influenced chunk can wrap the sum past HIGH_WATER, bypassing the P3 backpressure bound.
